questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सोवियत संघ का एक गणराज्य नहीं था ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following was not a republic of the Soviet Union ?
questions.solution: Afghanistan (option C) was never a republic of the Soviet Union. It was an independent country, though the USSR did invade and occupy it from 1979 to 1989. Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Azerbaijan were all constituent republics of the Soviet Union, which dissolved in 1991.
questions.solution_hindi: अफ़गानिस्तान (विकल्प C) कभी सोवियत संघ का गणराज्य नहीं था। यह एक स्वतंत्र देश था, हालांकि USSR ने 1979 से 1989 तक इस पर कब्जा किया था। ताजिकिस्तान, उज़्बेकिस्तान और अज़रबैजान सोवियत संघ के घटक गणराज्य थे जो 1991 में विघटित हुए।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन 1985 में सोवियत संघ की कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी का महासचिव था ?
questions.text_english: Who among the following was the General Secretary of the Communist Party of Soviet Union in 1985 ?
questions.solution: Mikhail Gorbachev (option B) became the General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union in March 1985. He introduced the famous policies of Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring). Stalin died in 1953, Khrushchev was deposed in 1964, and Brezhnev died in 1982.
questions.solution_hindi: मिखाइल गोर्बाचेव (विकल्प B) मार्च 1985 में सोवियत संघ की कम्युनिस्ट पार्टी के महासचिव बने। उन्होंने ग्लासनोस्त और पेरेस्त्रोइका नीतियां लागू कीं। स्टालिन की मृत्यु 1953 में, ख्रुश्चेव को 1964 में हटाया गया और ब्रेझनेव की मृत्यु 1982 में हुई।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : अप्रैल 2006 में नेपाल में पूरे देश में लोकतंत्र के पक्ष में स्वरोत प्रदर्शन हुए ।
कारण (R) : 2002 में राजा ने पार्लियामेंट को समाप्त कर के सरकार को भंग कर दिया था ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : In April 2006, there were massive countrywide pro-democracy protests in Nepal.
Reason (R) : In 2002, the king abolished the parliament and dismissed the government.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Choose the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). King Gyanendra of Nepal dismissed the government and dissolved parliament in 2002, concentrating power in his hands. This unconstitutional act led to growing public resentment, which culminated in the massive pro-democracy protests of April 2006 that forced the king to restore parliament.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है। नेपाल के राजा ज्ञानेंद्र ने 2002 में सरकार को बर्खास्त कर संसद को भंग कर दिया था। इसी असंवैधानिक कदम के कारण जनता में असंतोष बढ़ा जो अप्रैल 2006 के विशाल लोकतंत्र समर्थक प्रदर्शनों के रूप में सामने आया।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित का सही मिलान कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Match the following correctly :
questions.solution: The correct matching is option C: General Zia-ul-Haq was the military dictator of Pakistan (iii); Ziaur Rahman was the military ruler of Bangladesh (i); Rajapaksa was the President of Sri Lanka (iv); and the Seven Party Alliance was a coalition of political parties in Nepal that led the pro-democracy movement (ii).
questions.solution_hindi: सही मिलान विकल्प C है: जनरल ज़िया-उल-हक़ — पाकिस्तान (iii); ज़ियाउर रहमान — बांग्लादेश (i); राजपक्षे — श्रीलंका (iv); सेवेन पार्टी अलाएंस — नेपाल (ii)।

questions.text: दिए गए विकल्पों में से 'साल्ट' (SALT) संधि का सही विस्तृत रूप चुनिए :
questions.text_english: Choose the correct full form of the 'SALT' treaty from the options given below :
questions.solution: SALT stands for Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (option B). It was a series of bilateral agreements between the USA and USSR aimed at limiting the number of nuclear missiles and other strategic weapons held by both superpowers. SALT I was signed in 1972 and SALT II in 1979 during the Cold War era.
questions.solution_hindi: SALT का पूर्ण रूप Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (रणनीतिक शस्त्र सीमा संधि) है (विकल्प B)। यह अमेरिका और सोवियत संघ के बीच परमाणु हथियारों को सीमित करने के लिए की गई द्विपक्षीय संधि थी। SALT I 1972 में और SALT II 1979 में शीत युद्ध के दौरान हस्ताक्षरित हुई।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प सुरक्षा के लिए खतरे का एक नया स्रोत नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is not a new source of threat to security ?
questions.solution: War (option B) is not a new source of threat to security — it is a traditional or conventional source of security threat that has existed throughout history. Terrorism, poverty, and migration are considered new or non-traditional sources of threats to security that emerged with greater prominence in the post-Cold War period.
questions.solution_hindi: युद्ध (विकल्प B) सुरक्षा के लिए खतरे का नया स्रोत नहीं है — यह एक पारंपरिक या परंपरागत सुरक्षा खतरा है जो इतिहास में सदा से रहा है। आतंकवाद, गरीबी और प्रवास को शीत युद्ध के बाद उभरे नए या गैर-परंपरागत सुरक्षा खतरों के रूप में माना जाता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसने 'द्वि-राष्ट्र के सिद्धांत' को प्रस्तुत किया था ?
questions.text_english: Who among the following advanced the 'Two-nation theory' ?
questions.solution: The Two-Nation Theory was advanced by the Muslim League (option B) under the leadership of Muhammad Ali Jinnah. It argued that Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations with distinct cultures, religions, and ways of life, and therefore required two separate homelands. This theory provided the ideological basis for the partition of British India and the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
questions.solution_hindi: द्वि-राष्ट्र सिद्धांत को मुहम्मद अली जिन्ना के नेतृत्व में मुस्लिम लीग (विकल्प B) ने प्रस्तुत किया। इस सिद्धांत के अनुसार हिंदू और मुसलमान दो अलग राष्ट्र हैं जिनकी संस्कृति, धर्म और जीवनशैली भिन्न है। यही सिद्धांत 1947 में भारत के विभाजन और पाकिस्तान के निर्माण का वैचारिक आधार बना।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : 1947 में भारत की सीमा के दोनों तरफ हत्याएं और अत्याचार हुए ।
कारण (R) : जनसंख्या का नियोजित स्थानांतरण असफल हो चुका था ।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : There were killings and atrocities on both sides of the border of India in 1947.
Reason (R) : The planned transfer of the population had failed.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं – एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Choose the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परंतु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: Assertion (A) is true — the partition of 1947 did result in massive communal violence, killings, and atrocities on both sides of the border. However, Reason (R) is false — there was no planned or organised transfer of population. The migration was chaotic, sudden, and unplanned, which is precisely why it led to such widespread violence and suffering. Since R is false, option C is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) सही है — 1947 के विभाजन से सीमा के दोनों तरफ भारी सांप्रदायिक हिंसा, हत्याएं और अत्याचार हुए। किंतु कारण (R) गलत है — जनसंख्या का कोई नियोजित स्थानांतरण नहीं था। यह पलायन अव्यवस्थित, अचानक और अनियोजित था, जिसके कारण इतनी व्यापक हिंसा हुई। अतः विकल्प C सही है।

questions.text: 'नीति आयोग' कब अस्तित्व में आया ?
questions.text_english: 'NITI Aayog' came into existence on :
questions.solution: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) came into existence on 1st January, 2015 (option A). It replaced the Planning Commission, which had been established in 1950. NITI Aayog functions as a think tank and advisory body to the Government of India, promoting cooperative federalism and bottom-up policy planning.
questions.solution_hindi: नीति आयोग (National Institution for Transforming India) 1 जनवरी, 2015 (विकल्प A) को अस्तित्व में आया। इसने 1950 में स्थापित योजना आयोग का स्थान लिया। नीति आयोग भारत सरकार के एक थिंक टैंक और सलाहकार निकाय के रूप में कार्य करता है।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित घटनाओं को कालक्रमानुसार व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(i) पी.सी. महालनोबिस ने एक पंचवर्षीय योजना का नेतृत्व किया।
(ii) के.एन. राज को प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना का प्रारूप तैयार करने में शामिल किया गया था।
(iii) 'बॉम्बे प्लान' तैयार किया गया।
(iv) योजना आयोग की स्थापना की गई।
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following events in chronological order :
(i) P.C. Mahalanobis led a Five-Year Plan.
(ii) K.N. Raj was involved in drafting the First Five-Year Plan.
(iii) The 'Bombay Plan' was drafted.
(iv) The Planning Commission was set up.
questions.solution: The correct chronological order is option A: (iii), (iv), (ii), (i). The Bombay Plan was drafted in 1944–1945 by leading industrialists. The Planning Commission was set up in 1950. K.N. Raj helped draft the First Five-Year Plan (1951–56). P.C. Mahalanobis led the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61), which focused on heavy industry and became the dominant planning model.
questions.solution_hindi: सही कालक्रम विकल्प A है: (iii), (iv), (ii), (i)। 'बॉम्बे प्लान' 1944-45 में तैयार हुआ। योजना आयोग 1950 में स्थापित हुआ। के.एन. राज ने प्रथम पंचवर्षीय योजना (1951-56) का प्रारूप तैयार करने में सहयोग किया। पी.सी. महालनोबिस ने द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-61) का नेतृत्व किया जो भारी उद्योग पर केंद्रित थी।

questions.text: किस राजनीतिक पार्टी/गठबन्धन की सरकार ने मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशों को लागू करने का निर्णय लिया था ?
questions.text_english: The government of which political party/alliance decided to implement the recommendations of the Mandal Commission ?
questions.solution: The National Front government (option B) under Prime Minister V.P. Singh decided to implement the Mandal Commission recommendations in August 1990. The Mandal Commission had submitted its report in 1980, recommending 27% reservations for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in government jobs and educational institutions, but it remained unimplemented for a decade until V.P. Singh's government acted on it.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रधानमंत्री वी.पी. सिंह के नेतृत्व में नेशनल फ्रंट सरकार (विकल्प B) ने अगस्त 1990 में मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशों को लागू करने का निर्णय लिया। मंडल आयोग ने 1980 में अपनी रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत की थी जिसमें सरकारी नौकरियों और शैक्षणिक संस्थानों में अन्य पिछड़े वर्गों (OBC) को 27% आरक्षण देने की सिफारिश की गई थी।

questions.text: उस राजनीतिक पार्टी के नाम को चुनिए जिसकी विचारधारा गांधीवादी समाजवाद के साथ सांस्कृतिक राष्ट्रवाद की है ।
questions.text_english: Choose the name of that political party which has Gandhian Socialism along with cultural nationalism as its ideology.
questions.solution: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) (option D) combines Gandhian Socialism with cultural nationalism as its ideology. The BJP, which emerged from the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, espouses integral humanism and cultural nationalism (Hindutva) as its core ideological pillars, while also incorporating elements of Gandhian Socialism in its economic outlook. The Socialist Party was purely socialist, Janata Party had mixed ideology, and National Conference is a regional party of J&K.
questions.solution_hindi: भारतीय जनता पार्टी (BJP) (विकल्प D) की विचारधारा गांधीवादी समाजवाद के साथ सांस्कृतिक राष्ट्रवाद की है। BJP भारतीय जनसंघ से उभरी है और एकात्म मानवतावाद तथा सांस्कृतिक राष्ट्रवाद (हिंदुत्व) को अपने मूल वैचारिक स्तंभ मानती है।
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर

questions.text: संयुक्त राष्ट्र के किन्हीं चार प्रमुख अंगों के नाम लिखिए ।
questions.text_english: Name any four principal organs of the United Nations.

key_points: General Assembly
Security Council
International Court of Justice
Secretariat

questions.solution: The four principal organs of the United Nations are: (1) General Assembly — the main deliberative body with all member nations; (2) Security Council — responsible for maintaining international peace and security; (3) International Court of Justice — the principal judicial organ located at The Hague; and (4) Secretariat — the administrative body headed by the Secretary-General.
questions.solution_hindi: संयुक्त राष्ट्र के चार प्रमुख अंग हैं: (1) महासभा — सभी सदस्य देशों की प्रमुख विचार-विमर्श संस्था; (2) सुरक्षा परिषद — अंतर्राष्ट्रीय शांति एवं सुरक्षा बनाए रखने हेतु उत्तरदायी; (3) अंतर्राष्ट्रीय न्यायालय — द हेग में स्थित प्रमुख न्यायिक अंग; तथा (4) सचिवालय — महासचिव के नेतृत्व में प्रशासनिक निकाय।

questions.text: वैश्वीकरण का अर्थ स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain the meaning of globalisation.

key_points: Free flow of ideas, capital, goods, and people across national borders
Integration of world economies through trade and technology
Interdependence among nations

questions.solution: Globalisation refers to the process of increasing interconnectedness and interdependence among countries of the world through the free flow of ideas, capital, goods, services, and people across national boundaries. It involves the integration of national economies into a single global economy through trade, investment, technology, and information. Globalisation has accelerated significantly due to advances in communication and transportation technology.
questions.solution_hindi: वैश्वीकरण से आशय राष्ट्रीय सीमाओं के पार विचारों, पूंजी, वस्तुओं, सेवाओं और लोगों के स्वतंत्र प्रवाह के माध्यम से विश्व के देशों के बीच बढ़ती परस्पर संपर्कता और परस्परनिर्भरता की प्रक्रिया से है। इसमें व्यापार, निवेश, प्रौद्योगिकी और सूचना के माध्यम से राष्ट्रीय अर्थव्यवस्थाओं को एकल वैश्विक अर्थव्यवस्था में एकीकृत करना शामिल है।

questions.text: भारत में वैश्वीकरण के विरोध के किन्हीं दो कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Analyse any two reasons for resistance to globalisation in India.

key_points: Threat to domestic industries and farmers from multinational competition
Cultural domination by Western values threatening Indian identity

questions.solution: There are two major reasons for resistance to globalisation in India. First, globalisation is seen as a threat to domestic industries and small farmers, as multinational corporations with vast resources enter the Indian market and compete with local businesses, often driving them out. Second, critics argue that globalisation promotes Western cultural values and lifestyles, which threatens India's rich cultural traditions and national identity, leading to what is called cultural imperialism.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत में वैश्वीकरण के विरोध के दो प्रमुख कारण हैं। प्रथम, वैश्वीकरण को घरेलू उद्योगों और छोटे किसानों के लिए खतरा माना जाता है, क्योंकि विशाल संसाधनों वाली बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियां भारतीय बाजार में प्रवेश कर स्थानीय व्यवसायों को विस्थापित कर देती हैं। द्वितीय, आलोचकों का मानना है कि वैश्वीकरण पश्चिमी सांस्कृतिक मूल्यों को बढ़ावा देता है जो भारत की समृद्ध सांस्कृतिक परंपराओं एवं राष्ट्रीय पहचान के लिए खतरा है।

questions.text: जनसंघ की उस विचारधारा को दर्शाइए जो इसे अन्य पार्टियों से अलग करती है ।
questions.text_english: Show the ideology of the Jana Sangh that makes it different from other parties.

key_points: Cultural nationalism based on one country, one culture, one nation concept
Emphasis on Hinduism, Hindu culture, and Hindu traditions
Advocated for reunification of India and Pakistan

questions.solution: The Bharatiya Jana Sangh, founded by Syama Prasad Mookerjee in 1951, was distinct from other parties because of its ideology of cultural nationalism. It emphasised the concept of one country, one culture, and one nation, rooted in Hindu cultural and religious traditions. Unlike secular parties, Jana Sangh sought to build a strong and modern India by drawing on Hindu traditions, and it strongly opposed any separate treatment based on religion, advocating for a uniform civil code.
questions.solution_hindi: 1951 में श्यामा प्रसाद मुखर्जी द्वारा स्थापित भारतीय जनसंघ अपनी सांस्कृतिक राष्ट्रवाद की विचारधारा के कारण अन्य पार्टियों से अलग था। इसने एक देश, एक संस्कृति और एक राष्ट्र की अवधारणा पर जोर दिया जो हिंदू सांस्कृतिक एवं धार्मिक परंपराओं में निहित थी। यह पार्टी समान नागरिक संहिता की पक्षधर थी और धर्म के आधार पर विशेष व्यवहार का विरोध करती थी।
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर

questions.text: सामाजिक और विचारधारात्मक गठबंधन के रूप में कांग्रेस पार्टी की प्रकृति की किन्हीं दो विशेषताओं को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any two features of the nature of the Congress party as a social and ideological coalition.

key_points: Congress accommodated diverse groups including conservatives, liberals, and socialists
It represented all regions, religions, castes, and classes under one umbrella

questions.solution: The Congress party functioned as a social and ideological coalition in two important ways. First, it accommodated a wide spectrum of political ideologies within its fold — from conservatives and moderates to socialists and even those with communitarian views — making it an ideological umbrella organisation. Second, it represented a broad social coalition cutting across regions, religions, castes, and classes, ensuring that virtually every section of Indian society found representation within the Congress, which helped it dominate electoral politics for decades.
questions.solution_hindi: कांग्रेस पार्टी दो महत्वपूर्ण तरीकों से सामाजिक और विचारधारात्मक गठबंधन के रूप में कार्य करती थी। प्रथम, इसने रूढ़िवादियों से लेकर समाजवादियों तक विभिन्न राजनीतिक विचारधाराओं को अपने अंदर समाहित किया जिससे यह एक वैचारिक छाता संगठन बन गई। द्वितीय, यह क्षेत्रों, धर्मों, जातियों और वर्गों के पार एक व्यापक सामाजिक गठबंधन का प्रतिनिधित्व करती थी।
questions.chapter: एक दल के प्रभुत्व का दौर

questions.text: अगस्त 1990 में मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशों को लागू करने के किन्हीं दो तात्कालिक परिणामों की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Explain any two immediate consequences of the implementation of the recommendations of the Mandal Commission in August 1990.

key_points: Massive anti-reservation protests by upper caste youth, including self-immolation incidents
Political crisis — BJP withdrew support from V.P. Singh government, leading to its fall

questions.solution: The implementation of the Mandal Commission recommendations in August 1990 had two major immediate consequences. First, it triggered massive nationwide anti-reservation protests by upper caste students and youth, with several young people resorting to self-immolation in desperation, leading to widespread social unrest and communal tension across the country. Second, it caused a severe political crisis as the BJP withdrew its outside support from V.P. Singh's National Front government, which ultimately led to the collapse of the government and mid-term elections.
questions.solution_hindi: अगस्त 1990 में मंडल आयोग की सिफारिशें लागू होने के दो प्रमुख तात्कालिक परिणाम हुए। प्रथम, उच्च जाति के छात्रों और युवाओं ने देशव्यापी आरक्षण विरोधी आंदोलन छेड़ दिया, कई युवाओं ने आत्मदाह का प्रयास किया जिससे व्यापक सामाजिक अशांति फैली। द्वितीय, भाजपा ने वी.पी. सिंह सरकार से समर्थन वापस ले लिया जिससे सरकार गिर गई और मध्यावधि चुनाव हुए।

questions.text:
(क) "भारत-रूस के संबंध आपसी विश्वास और साझा हितों के इतिहास में रचे बसे हैं ।" चार उदाहरणों के साथ इस कथन का समर्थन कीजिए ।
अथवा
(ख) "सोवियत प्रणाली लोगों का कल्याण सुनिश्चित करने के लिए थी ।" चार उदाहरणों के साथ इस कथन का समर्थन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) "Indo-Russian relations are embedded in the history of trust and common interests." Support the statement with four examples.
OR
(b) "Soviet system was to ensure the welfare of the people." Support the statement with four examples.

key_points: (a) Russia has been a consistent supplier of defence equipment and technology to India
(a) Both countries have cooperated in space exploration under ISRO-Roscosmos agreements
(a) India and Russia share a common concern about Islamic fundamentalism and terrorism in Asia
(a) Russia has supported India on key diplomatic issues such as Kashmir and India's permanent UNSC membership

questions.solution:
Indo-Russian relations are deeply rooted in shared trust and mutual interests, as demonstrated by four key examples. First, Russia has been India's most reliable defence partner, consistently supplying advanced weapons systems such as fighter aircraft, submarines, and missiles, including the BrahMos cruise missile developed jointly. Second, Russia supported India during critical moments, such as during the 1971 war with Pakistan, when the Soviet Union used its Security Council veto to prevent international intervention against India. Third, both nations have cooperated in civilian nuclear energy, with Russia assisting in the construction of nuclear reactors at Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu. Fourth, on diplomatic issues like India's permanent membership in the UN Security Council, Russia has been a consistent supporter, reflecting the long-standing strategic partnership between the two nations.

OR

The Soviet system was designed to ensure the welfare of its people in four significant ways. First, the Soviet state guaranteed employment to all citizens — there was virtually no unemployment in the USSR, as the government was committed to providing jobs to everyone. Second, the state ensured free and universal education for all citizens from elementary school through higher education, creating one of the most literate populations in the world. Third, free healthcare was provided to all Soviet citizens through a comprehensive public health system, ensuring basic medical facilities were accessible to everyone regardless of income. Fourth, the Soviet government heavily subsidised housing and essential commodities, ensuring that basic needs of food, shelter, and clothing were met for all people, thereby eliminating extreme poverty.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत-रूस संबंध साझा विश्वास और पारस्परिक हितों में गहराई से निहित हैं, जिसे चार उदाहरणों से स्पष्ट किया जा सकता है। प्रथम, रूस भारत का सबसे विश्वसनीय रक्षा भागीदार रहा है जिसने संयुक्त रूप से विकसित ब्रह्मोस क्रूज मिसाइल सहित उन्नत हथियार प्रणालियां प्रदान की हैं। द्वितीय, 1971 के भारत-पाक युद्ध के दौरान सोवियत संघ ने भारत के विरुद्ध अंतर्राष्ट्रीय हस्तक्षेप को रोकने के लिए सुरक्षा परिषद में अपने वीटो का उपयोग किया। तृतीय, रूस ने तमिलनाडु में कुडनकुलम परमाणु संयंत्र निर्माण में सहयोग किया। चतुर्थ, संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद में भारत की स्थायी सदस्यता के मुद्दे पर रूस लगातार समर्थक रहा है।

questions.text: शीत युद्ध की समाप्ति के बाद विश्व में आए किन्हीं चार परिवर्तनों का वर्णन कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Describe any four changes that occurred in the world after the end of the Cold War.

key_points: Emergence of a unipolar world with the USA as the sole superpower
Disintegration of the Soviet Union into 15 independent states
Rise of new nations in Eastern Europe and Central Asia
Shift from ideology-based to economics-based international relations

questions.solution: The end of the Cold War in 1991 brought about four significant changes in the world. First, the bipolar world order was replaced by a unipolar order dominated by the United States, which emerged as the sole superpower with unmatched military, economic, and cultural influence across the globe. Second, the Soviet Union disintegrated into 15 independent republics, creating new nations in Eastern Europe and Central Asia such as Ukraine, Belarus, Kazakhstan, and the Baltic states, which fundamentally redrew the political map of the world. Third, the ideological conflict between capitalism and communism came to an end, allowing countries to pursue mixed economic models, and international relations shifted from ideological confrontation to economic competition and cooperation. Fourth, there was a wave of democratisation across Eastern Europe and parts of Asia and Africa, as many authoritarian regimes that had been backed by either superpower transitioned to democratic forms of government.
questions.solution_hindi: 1991 में शीत युद्ध की समाप्ति ने विश्व में चार महत्वपूर्ण परिवर्तन लाए। प्रथम, द्विध्रुवीय विश्व व्यवस्था के स्थान पर एकध्रुवीय व्यवस्था आई जिसमें अमेरिका एकमात्र महाशक्ति के रूप में उभरा। द्वितीय, सोवियत संघ 15 स्वतंत्र गणराज्यों में विघटित हो गया। तृतीय, पूंजीवाद और साम्यवाद के बीच वैचारिक संघर्ष समाप्त हुआ और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संबंध आर्थिक प्रतिस्पर्धा की ओर स्थानांतरित हुए। चतुर्थ, पूर्वी यूरोप और एशिया के कई देशों में लोकतंत्रीकरण की लहर आई।

questions.text: किसी देश की सुरक्षा को संभावित युद्ध से खतरा होने पर उसके पास उपलब्ध किन्हीं चार विकल्पों को उजागर कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Highlight any four choices available to a state when its security is threatened by a possible war.

key_points: Surrender to avoid greater harm
Deterrence — making cost of attack too high through military buildup
Form alliances with other countries for collective security
Strengthen internal capability through economic and military development

questions.solution: When a state's security is threatened by a possible war, it has four main choices available. First, it may choose to surrender and accept the attacker's terms to prevent greater destruction, though this is the least preferred option as it may lead to loss of sovereignty. Second, a state can pursue deterrence by building up its military strength to such a level that the cost of attacking it becomes unacceptably high for the potential aggressor, thereby preventing war through the threat of retaliation. Third, the state can form alliances with other nations, creating a collective security arrangement so that an attack on one is treated as an attack on all, thereby increasing the state's security through cooperative defence. Fourth, a state can work to strengthen its internal capabilities by investing in economic development, technology, and human resources, making itself strong enough to resist any external threat over the long term.
questions.solution_hindi: जब किसी देश की सुरक्षा को संभावित युद्ध से खतरा हो तो उसके पास चार मुख्य विकल्प होते हैं। प्रथम, अधिक विनाश से बचने के लिए आत्मसमर्पण कर आक्रमणकारी की शर्तें मान लेना, हालांकि यह सबसे कम पसंदीदा विकल्प है। द्वितीय, सैन्य शक्ति का निर्माण कर प्रतिरोध स्थापित करना ताकि आक्रमण की कीमत इतनी अधिक हो जाए कि शत्रु हमला करने से डरे। तृतीय, सामूहिक सुरक्षा के लिए अन्य देशों के साथ गठबंधन बनाना। चतुर्थ, आर्थिक विकास, प्रौद्योगिकी और मानव संसाधन में निवेश कर आंतरिक क्षमताओं को मजबूत करना।

questions.text:
(क) 1967 के चुनावों के बाद कांग्रेस पार्टी में विभाजन के किन्हीं दो प्रमुख कारणों को स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
अथवा
(ख) पांचवें आम चुनावों से पूर्व प्रधानमंत्री इन्दिरा गांधी की लोकप्रियता के कोई चार कारण स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain any two major reasons for the split in the Congress party after the 1967 elections.
OR
(b) Explain any four reasons for the popularity of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi before the fifth general elections.

key_points: (a) Conflict between the Syndicate (old guard) and Indira Gandhi over party ideology and leadership
(a) Indira Gandhi's leftward shift and radical economic policies like bank nationalisation opposed by conservatives
(b) Garibi Hatao slogan connected her with the poor masses
(b) Bank nationalisation projected her as pro-poor leader

questions.solution:
The split in the Congress party after 1967 occurred due to two major reasons. First, there was a fundamental conflict between the old guard of the party called the Syndicate, led by leaders like S. Nijalingappa and Kamaraj, and Indira Gandhi. The Syndicate wanted to control the government through party organisation, while Indira Gandhi sought independent authority and resisted the Syndicate's dominance. This power struggle became irreconcilable. Second, Indira Gandhi adopted a distinctly leftist economic stance, advocating radical policies like nationalisation of banks, abolition of privy purses, and pro-poor programmes, which were strongly opposed by the conservative faction within the party. This ideological divergence ultimately led to a formal split in 1969, creating Congress (R) led by Indira Gandhi and Congress (O) led by the Syndicate.

OR

Indira Gandhi's popularity before the fifth general elections (1971) was rooted in four important factors. First, her powerful and emotionally resonant slogan 'Garibi Hatao' (Remove Poverty) directly appealed to the vast majority of poor Indians and gave them a sense of hope, creating a personal bond between her and the masses. Second, her decision to nationalise fourteen major banks in 1969 was seen as a bold pro-poor measure that protected common people's savings and extended credit to the agricultural sector, which greatly enhanced her image as a champion of the poor. Third, her victory in the 1971 war with Pakistan and the creation of Bangladesh projected her as a strong and decisive national leader, earning her the title 'Durga' from the opposition. Fourth, she successfully projected the 1971 elections as a contest between her and the reactionary opposition, creating a wave of sympathy and support in her favour by positioning herself as the voice of the poor and marginalised.
questions.solution_hindi: 1967 के बाद कांग्रेस पार्टी में विभाजन के दो प्रमुख कारण थे। प्रथम, पुराने नेताओं के समूह 'सिंडिकेट' (एस. निजलिंगप्पा, कामराज) और इन्दिरा गांधी के बीच नेतृत्व एवं पार्टी नियंत्रण को लेकर गहरा टकराव था। द्वितीय, इन्दिरा गांधी ने बैंकों के राष्ट्रीयकरण जैसी वामपंथी आर्थिक नीतियां अपनाईं जिनका रूढ़िवादी गुट ने विरोध किया। इन दो कारणों से 1969 में पार्टी विभाजित होकर कांग्रेस (आर) और कांग्रेस (ओ) में बंट गई।

questions.text: क्या 1975 में घोषित आपातकाल आवश्यक था ? अपने उत्तर के पक्ष में दो तर्क दीजिए ।
questions.text_english: Was the Emergency declared in 1975 necessary ? Support your answer with two arguments.

key_points: For (necessary): Political instability and JP movement threatened constitutional order
Against (not necessary): Used to suppress political opposition and democratic rights
Emergency led to abuse of power and violation of civil liberties

questions.solution: The Emergency declared in 1975 was a deeply controversial decision. Those who argue it was not necessary offer the following two arguments. First, the government misused Emergency powers to suppress legitimate political opposition, impose censorship on the press, and arrest thousands of opposition leaders without trial under MISA. This demonstrated that the intent was to protect Indira Gandhi's personal political power rather than address any genuine national emergency. Second, the Allahabad High Court judgment finding Indira Gandhi guilty of electoral malpractice was a judicial matter to be resolved through proper legal channels, not through the suspension of democracy. The opposition movement led by Jayaprakash Narayan was a peaceful democratic movement, not an armed insurrection threatening the constitutional order, making the proclamation of emergency disproportionate and unjustified.
questions.solution_hindi: 1975 में घोषित आपातकाल एक अत्यंत विवादास्पद निर्णय था। जो लोग कहते हैं कि यह अनावश्यक था, वे दो तर्क देते हैं। प्रथम, सरकार ने आपातकालीन शक्तियों का दुरुपयोग कर वैध राजनीतिक विपक्ष को दबाया, प्रेस पर सेंसरशिप लगाई और हजारों विपक्षी नेताओं को बिना मुकदमे के जेल भेजा। यह दर्शाता है कि इरादा राष्ट्रीय संकट से निपटना नहीं बल्कि इन्दिरा गांधी की व्यक्तिगत सत्ता की रक्षा करना था। द्वितीय, जयप्रकाश नारायण के नेतृत्व में विपक्षी आंदोलन एक शांतिपूर्ण लोकतांत्रिक आंदोलन था, कोई सशस्त्र विद्रोह नहीं, इसलिए आपातकाल की घोषणा अनावश्यक और असंगत थी।

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अवतरण को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़िए और इस पर आधारित प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए :
"1989 में कांग्रेस पार्टी की हार ने भारत की दलीय व्यवस्था में कांग्रेस के प्रभुत्व का अन्त चिह्नित किया। हालांकि इसका अर्थ कांग्रेस पार्टी का स्थान लेने के लिए किसी अन्य दल का उदय नहीं था। इस प्रकार बहुदलीय प्रणाली का युग शुरू हुआ जिसमें क्षेत्रीय पार्टियों ने गठबन्धन बनाने में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई।"
questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on it :
"The defeat of the Congress party in 1989 marked the end of Congress dominance over the Indian party system. It did not, however, mean the emergence of any other single party to fill in its place. Thus, began an era of multi-party system, in which regional parties played a crucial role in forming the alliances."

sub_questions.text: कौन-से वर्ष कांग्रेस पार्टी को पहली बार झटका लगा और कुछ राज्यों में सत्ता खोनी पड़ी ?
sub_questions.text_english: In which year did the Congress party face a setback for the first time and lose power in some states ?
sub_questions.solution: In 1967, the Congress party faced its first major electoral setback. Although it retained power at the Centre, it lost to opposition parties in several states including Rajasthan, Bihar, Orissa, UP, West Bengal, Madras, and Punjab, marking the beginning of the end of one-party dominance.

sub_questions.text: किस राजनीतिक पार्टी/गठबंधन ने दिसम्बर 1989 में पहली गठबन्धन की सरकार बनाई थी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which political party/alliance formed the first coalition government in December 1989 ?
sub_questions.solution: The National Front, a coalition led by V.P. Singh of the Janata Dal, formed the first coalition government at the Centre in December 1989 after the 1989 general elections. It was supported from outside by the BJP and the Left parties.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से क्षेत्रीय दल ने किसी भी राज्य में कभी कोई सरकार नहीं बनाई ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which one of the following regional parties never formed a government in any state ?
sub_questions.solution: The Bharatiya Kranti Dal (BKD) never formed a government in any state. The DMK has governed Tamil Nadu multiple times, the Shiromani Akali Dal has governed Punjab, and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) has formed governments in Uttar Pradesh.

sub_questions.text: 1989 के चुनावों के बाद लोक सभा में कौन-सी पार्टी सबसे बड़ी पार्टी थी ?
sub_questions.text_english: Which party was the largest party in the Lok Sabha after the 1989 elections ?
sub_questions.solution: Even after its defeat in 1989, the Indian National Congress remained the single largest party in the Lok Sabha with 197 seats. However, it chose to sit in opposition rather than form the government, allowing V.P. Singh's National Front to form the coalition government.

questions.text_english:
In the given political outline map of India, four States have been marked as A, B, C and D. Identify these States on the basis of the information given below :
(i) The state which was bifurcated between India and Pakistan at the time of the partition.
(ii) The state which was created in 1966.
(iii) The state to which the first Deputy Prime Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel belonged.
(iv) The state to which Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh belonged.

key_points: (i) C — Punjab (bifurcated at partition into Indian Punjab and Pakistani Punjab)
(ii) C or nearby — Haryana (created in 1966 from Punjab's reorganisation)
(iii) B — Gujarat (Sardar Patel's home state)
(iv) A — Manipur (Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed the Instrument of Accession)

questions.solution: Based on the map, the four states are identified as follows. (i) Serial number (i) corresponds to alphabet C — Punjab. At the time of partition in 1947, the province of Punjab was divided between India and Pakistan, with Indian Punjab going to India and West Punjab becoming part of Pakistan. (ii) Serial number (ii) corresponds to a state in the northwest region — Haryana. Haryana was carved out of the Punjab state on 1 November 1966 on a linguistic basis, as Punjabi-speaking areas were separated from Hindi-speaking areas. (iii) Serial number (iii) corresponds to alphabet B — Gujarat. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, India's first Deputy Prime Minister and the Iron Man of India, hailed from Nadiad in present-day Gujarat. (iv) Serial number (iv) corresponds to alphabet A — Manipur. Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh was the ruler of the princely state of Manipur who signed the Instrument of Accession with India in 1949.

Study the cartoon given below and answer the questions based on it :
Note: The man shown in the suit is President Musharraf and the same man shown in the cap is General Musharraf. On the basis of politics in Pakistan, answer the following questions.
(i) What message is given by the uppermost equation ? Explain.
(ii) Explain the message given by the middle line.

sub_questions.text: सबसे ऊपर दिया गया समीकरण क्या सन्देश देता है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: What message is given by the uppermost equation ? Explain.

key_points: President Musharraf minus General Musharraf equals zero — Musharraf as civilian president has no independent power without military backing

sub_questions.solution: The uppermost equation shows: President Musharraf minus General Musharraf equals zero. This conveys the message that Pervez Musharraf as a civilian President has no real power or legitimacy on his own. His authority as President is entirely dependent on and derived from his position as the Army General. Without his military role, he is nothing — his presidency is hollow and meaningless without the army's backing.

sub_questions.text: बीच की पंक्ति के समीकरण का सन्देश स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the message given by the middle line.

key_points: General Musharraf minus President Musharraf equals 1 — without the presidential facade, the General alone is the real power

sub_questions.solution: The middle equation shows: General Musharraf minus President Musharraf equals one. This conveys the message that the true and only source of power in Pakistan is the military General. When the civilian presidential facade (President Musharraf) is removed, what remains is one powerful entity — the military general who actually controls everything. Real power in Pakistan lies with the army, not the elected or appointed civilian leadership.

sub_questions.text: सबसे नीचे की लाइन का सन्देश स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the message given by the lowest line.

key_points: President plus General equals 2 — same person wearing two hats, doubling his power and control

sub_questions.solution: The lowest equation shows: President Musharraf plus General Musharraf equals two. This conveys the message that Musharraf was simultaneously wearing two hats — he held both the office of the President (civilian authority) and the position of Army Chief (military authority) at the same time. By combining both roles in one person, he doubled his power and had unchecked control over both the civilian government and the military machinery of Pakistan.

sub_questions.text: पूरे कार्टून द्वारा दिए गए सन्देश को उजागर कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Highlight the message conveyed by the whole cartoon.

key_points: Military dominates civilian authority in Pakistan
Democracy is a facade over military dictatorship

sub_questions.solution: The overall message of the cartoon is that in Pakistan, genuine democracy has never truly existed because the military has always remained the real seat of power. Musharraf's presidency was a sham — it was just a civilian mask worn over a military dictatorship. The cartoon satirises Pakistan's political reality where the army uses democratic institutions as tools to legitimise its control, and a general can wear a suit and call himself a president, but the underlying reality remains one of military rule. Musharraf himself boasted about being good at 'calculation', suggesting he cleverly manipulated both roles to maintain absolute authority.

questions.text_english:
(a) Analyse any four decisions made by the Chinese leadership that led to the rise of the Chinese economy.
OR
(b) Analyse any four reasons that make the European Union an influential regional organisation.

key_points: (a) Normalisation of relations with USA in 1972 opened doors to Western markets
(a) Dismantling of collective farming and allowing private enterprise in agriculture (1978 reforms)
(a) Establishment of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) to attract foreign investment
(a) Joining WTO in 2001 integrated China into global trade

questions.solution:
Four key decisions by Chinese leadership that drove the rise of the Chinese economy are as follows.

First, in 1978, Deng Xiaoping introduced the historic 'Open Door Policy' and economic reforms that dismantled collective farming, allowed farmers to sell surplus produce in the market, and introduced elements of a market economy alongside state planning. This agricultural decollectivisation dramatically increased rural incomes and food production.

Second, the Chinese leadership established Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in coastal regions like Shenzhen, where foreign investment was welcomed, taxes were reduced, and companies could operate with less bureaucratic interference. These SEZs became engines of export-led growth and technology transfer, attracting billions in foreign direct investment.

Third, China normalised its relations with the United States in 1972 under Mao Zedong and Nixon, which opened access to Western markets, technology, and capital. This diplomatic realignment was crucial for China's subsequent integration into the global economy.

Fourth, China joined the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in 2001, which gave it permanent access to global markets and accelerated its export-driven manufacturing boom. Combined with a massive, low-cost labour force, this turned China into the world's factory, making it the second largest economy in the world.

OR

Four reasons that make the European Union an influential regional organisation are as follows.

First, the European Union is the world's largest trading bloc with a combined GDP comparable to that of the United States. It negotiates trade agreements on behalf of all its member states as a single entity, giving it enormous economic leverage in global trade negotiations that no individual member state could achieve alone.

Second, the EU has its own currency, the Euro, used by 20 of its member states. The Euro is the second most widely used reserve currency in the world after the US dollar, giving the EU significant monetary influence over global financial markets and reducing transaction costs within the Eurozone.

Third, the EU exercises considerable political and diplomatic influence. It speaks with one voice on many international issues, has a common foreign and security policy, and its decisions on sanctions, trade, and human rights carry significant weight in international forums including the United Nations.

Fourth, the EU's military capabilities, though not unified under a single command, are substantial. EU member states collectively spend significant amounts on defence, and the EU has undertaken peacekeeping and conflict prevention missions in various parts of the world, establishing itself as an important actor in global security.
questions.solution_hindi: चीन की अर्थव्यवस्था के उत्थान में चार प्रमुख निर्णयों की भूमिका रही। प्रथम, 1978 में देंग श्याओपिंग ने 'खुले द्वार की नीति' और आर्थिक सुधार लागू किए जिसमें सामूहिक खेती को समाप्त कर किसानों को बाजार में अधिशेष बेचने की अनुमति दी। द्वितीय, तटीय क्षेत्रों में विशेष आर्थिक क्षेत्र (SEZ) स्थापित किए जहां विदेशी निवेश को प्रोत्साहित किया गया। तृतीय, 1972 में अमेरिका के साथ संबंध सामान्य किए जिससे पश्चिमी बाजारों तक पहुंच संभव हुई। चतुर्थ, 2001 में WTO में शामिल होने से वैश्विक व्यापार में एकीकरण हुआ।

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the concept of 'common but differentiated responsibilities' to conserve, protect and restore the health of the environment.
OR
(b) Explain any four steps taken by the Government of India to save the environment from degradation.

key_points: All nations share responsibility for environmental protection
Developed nations bear greater responsibility as historical polluters
Developing nations need financial and technological support
Different obligations based on capability and historical contribution to pollution

questions.solution:
The principle of 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) is a foundational concept in international environmental law, first articulated in the Rio Declaration of 1992. It recognises two interconnected truths about the global environmental crisis.

On one hand, it acknowledges that environmental protection is a shared or common responsibility of all nations. Since the Earth's atmosphere, oceans, and ecosystems are shared resources, every country has a stake in and an obligation to protect the global environment from degradation. No country can be exempted from this common responsibility.

On the other hand, the principle recognises that responsibilities are differentiated — meaning they are not equal for all countries. Developed nations like the USA, European countries, and Japan have historically been responsible for the bulk of industrial pollution, greenhouse gas emissions, and resource depletion over the past two centuries. They therefore bear a greater and more urgent responsibility to lead environmental restoration efforts, reduce emissions, and provide financial resources and technology to developing nations.

Developing countries like India and China, while also obligated to protect the environment, argue that they need the freedom to industrialise and develop economically. They cannot be held to the same strict emission-reduction targets as wealthy nations that already industrialised using cheap fossil fuels. Under CBDR, rich nations are expected to provide financial assistance and transfer clean technologies to help developing nations grow sustainably. This principle has been central to all major climate negotiations including the Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement.

OR

The Government of India has taken four important steps to protect the environment from degradation. First, India has enacted strong environmental legislation, including the Environment Protection Act of 1986, the Air Prevention and Control of Pollution Act, and the Water Act, creating a legal framework to regulate industrial pollution and hold polluters accountable. The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in 2010 as a specialised court for environmental cases. Second, India has committed to ambitious renewable energy targets, pledging to achieve 500 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030 under its Nationally Determined Contributions to the Paris Agreement. India is rapidly expanding solar power through initiatives like the National Solar Mission, making it one of the world's largest solar energy producers. Third, India has launched the National Action Plan on Climate Change, which includes eight national missions covering solar energy, energy efficiency, sustainable agriculture, and water conservation. This comprehensive plan addresses climate adaptation and mitigation across multiple sectors simultaneously. Fourth, India has joined international environmental initiatives and agreements, including the Paris Agreement, and has championed the International Solar Alliance with France to promote solar energy globally. India has also committed to protecting and increasing its forest cover as a carbon sink, with various afforestation programmes being implemented across the country.
questions.solution_hindi: 'साझी परन्तु अलग-अलग जिम्मेदारियों' का सिद्धांत 1992 के रियो घोषणापत्र में प्रतिपादित किया गया। इसके अनुसार पर्यावरण संरक्षण सभी देशों की साझी जिम्मेदारी है, किंतु ऐतिहासिक प्रदूषण में अधिक भागीदारी के कारण विकसित देशों की जिम्मेदारी अधिक है। विकासशील देशों को अपने विकास की भी जरूरत है और उन्हें वही कठोर मानकों पर नहीं रखा जा सकता जो विकसित देशों पर लागू हों। अतः विकसित देशों का दायित्व है कि वे प्रौद्योगिकी और वित्तीय सहायता विकासशील देशों को दें।

questions.text_english:
(a) Explain any three reasons that are responsible for the strained relations between India and China.
OR
(b) Explain any three important features of India's Nuclear Policy.

key_points: (a) Border dispute over McMahon Line and Aksai Chin leading to 1962 war
(a) China's support for Pakistan including nuclear and missile technology
(a) China's growing presence in Indian Ocean (String of Pearls policy)

questions.solution:
Three major reasons responsible for strained relations between India and China are as follows.

First, the unresolved border dispute is the most fundamental source of tension. India and China share a long and disputed boundary. China claims Arunachal Pradesh as 'South Tibet' and the two countries fought a brief but humiliating war in 1962 over the border. The Line of Actual Control (LAC) remains contentious, with frequent transgressions and military stand-offs such as the Doklam standoff in 2017 and the Galwan Valley clash in 2020. This border dispute has cast a long shadow over bilateral relations.

Second, China's strategic partnership with Pakistan is a major irritant for India. China has been a key supplier of nuclear technology, missile systems, and conventional weapons to Pakistan, which India considers a direct threat to its security. China's consistent support for Pakistan at international forums, including blocking India's attempts to designate Pakistani terrorists through the UN Security Council, deepens India's suspicion of Chinese intentions.

Third, China's 'String of Pearls' strategy — establishing a network of ports and military facilities in countries surrounding India such as Pakistan (Gwadar), Sri Lanka (Hambantota), Bangladesh, and Myanmar — is seen by India as an attempt to encircle India strategically and expand Chinese naval influence deep into the Indian Ocean region, which India considers its primary sphere of maritime influence.

OR

Three important features of India's Nuclear Policy are as follows.

First, India follows a policy of No First Use (NFU), meaning India has pledged that it will never be the first to use nuclear weapons in any conflict. India will only use nuclear weapons in retaliation if it or its allies are attacked with nuclear weapons. This policy is aimed at reducing the risk of nuclear war and presenting India as a responsible nuclear power committed to restraint and non-aggression.

Second, India has maintained a policy of minimum credible deterrence. India does not seek to build the largest possible nuclear arsenal but only maintains the minimum number of nuclear weapons necessary to deter any potential nuclear attack by its adversaries. This approach balances India's security needs with financial prudence and reflects a commitment to not engaging in a nuclear arms race.

Third, India remains committed to global nuclear disarmament and has consistently called for the elimination of all nuclear weapons worldwide. India refused to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) because it considered the treaty discriminatory — it allowed the five permanent UN Security Council members to retain their nuclear arsenals while preventing others from developing them. India argues for a universal, non-discriminatory approach to disarmament where all nations, including the nuclear powers, give up their weapons.
questions.solution_hindi: भारत और चीन के बीच तनावपूर्ण संबंधों के तीन प्रमुख कारण हैं। प्रथम, सीमा विवाद — चीन अरुणाचल प्रदेश को 'दक्षिण तिब्बत' बताता है और 1962 में दोनों देशों के बीच युद्ध भी हो चुका है। LAC पर बार-बार घुसपैठ होती रहती है जैसे 2020 में गलवान घाटी संघर्ष। द्वितीय, पाकिस्तान को चीन द्वारा परमाणु और मिसाइल तकनीक की आपूर्ति तथा अंतर्राष्ट्रीय मंचों पर पाकिस्तान का समर्थन। तृतीय, 'स्ट्रिंग ऑफ पर्ल्स' रणनीति — पाकिस्तान, श्रीलंका, म्यांमार में बंदरगाह बनाकर भारत को घेरने की कोशिश।

questions.text_english:
(a) 'Regional aspirations and demands are part and parcel of democratic politics.' Support the statement with three examples.
OR
(b) Suggest any three measures to strengthen 'unity in diversity' in India.

key_points: (a) Punjab accord resolving Sikh regional demands
(a) Reorganisation of states on linguistic basis satisfying regional aspirations
(a) Mizoram peace accord bringing insurgent groups into mainstream democracy

questions.solution:
Regional aspirations and demands are indeed an integral part of democratic politics, as demonstrated by the following three examples from Indian political history.

First, the States Reorganisation Act of 1956 is a landmark example of the democratic system accommodating regional aspirations. Movements across the country demanded that states be organised along linguistic lines, with Potti Sriramulu's fast unto death for a separate Telugu-speaking state being the most dramatic instance. The Indian government eventually accepted these demands and reorganised states on a linguistic basis, recognising that regional identities are legitimate within a democratic framework. This democratic accommodation of regional aspirations actually strengthened national unity.

Second, the Punjab crisis of the 1980s and the subsequent Punjab Accord of 1985 (Rajiv-Longowal Accord) demonstrate how regional demands — including demands for Chandigarh as Punjab's capital and river water sharing — were addressed through democratic negotiation. The Akali Dal's regional demands, though they escalated into violent militancy, were ultimately resolved through democratic dialogue, showing that regional aspirations can and must be accommodated within the democratic process.

Third, the Mizoram Accord of 1986 is perhaps the most successful example. The Mizo National Front, which had been waging an armed insurgency for independence, was brought into the mainstream through democratic negotiations. Laldenga, the MNF leader, signed a peace accord with the Indian government and subsequently became the Chief Minister of Mizoram through democratic elections. This shows that even the most extreme regional aspirations can be accommodated within democracy, turning separatist movements into participants in the democratic process.

OR

Three measures to strengthen unity in diversity in India are as follows.

First, promoting inter-state dialogue and cultural exchange is essential. The government should actively organise and support festivals, exchange programmes, and cultural events that showcase India's diverse traditions, languages, and customs to people across the country. When Indians from different regions understand and appreciate each other's cultures, it builds a sense of shared national identity that transcends regional and community differences.

Second, the equitable distribution of economic development across all states and regions is crucial to preventing feelings of regional discrimination that can fuel separatism. The government should prioritise reducing regional economic disparities through special development packages for backward states and regions, ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reach the remotest corners of the country. People who feel economically marginalised are more likely to develop strong grievances that can be exploited by forces working against national unity.

Third, strengthening federal institutions and ensuring that state governments have adequate autonomy and resources is vital. When regional governments feel empowered and believe that their concerns are heard and addressed through constitutional mechanisms, it reduces the sense of alienation that often drives regional movements. A strong federal structure where Centre-state relations are cooperative rather than adversarial creates a political environment in which diverse regions can coexist harmoniously within the framework of one nation.
